evals.prompt: Hi! I'm 29 and work as a data analyst at a bank. I write Excel formulas and macros and know SQL. I studied textile engineering. I used to play the lute in high school and still play occasionally. I've never drawn anything. I installed Blender twice and closed it when I saw all the panels. I downloaded Godot, watched a few videos, and couldn't wrap my head around nodes and scenes. Everyone on YouTube says 'just make a small game right away.' I really want to make games—where should I start? Also, I'm not a CS major: Unreal or Unity?
evals.expected_output: Skill inventory mapped to the three foundations, per-foundation status, one concrete next step, and a direct answer to the engine question.
expectations: Inventory uses valid domains and levels and scripts/skill_inventory.py runs without errors
All three foundations (balanced composition, complexity tolerance, practical developer skill) are reported separately
One clear next step is recommended consistent with the script's Next Step section
User is reassured that having a narrow or non-game background is normal and not discouraged from making games
The Unreal vs. Unity engine question is answered directly without being blocked
Response is written in English and saved to outputs/response.md
